title: MCA exploits Herbie Fields until Joe Glazer places him with Hampton
summary: Cobb relates how MCA bled Fields's family out of $80,000 for air time and passed him over for another act until Joe Glazer rescued him and put him with Hampton at $250 a week.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: So they put him in New Jersey at the Meadowbrook -- what is it? Daly, Frank Daly? Meadowbrook, and they had Herbert playing for air time. They bled Herbert and his mother's husband, who's a jeweler in Newark, New Jersey, out of $80,000.00. But they were doing all this. And Herbert, see, what was happening, in order to keep his band together, he would rehearse during the week. And what happened, instead of him paying full, he paid everybody half salary anyway because he was rehearsing them and they wasn't getting no jobs for them and they put him back in Frank Daly Meadowbrook. That's the only place he could work, pay for the air time and get published.
Invited the secretary in MCA's office out to lunch, said he was going to invest $10.00 on her to find out.

He talked to her confidentially. And this is what they was telling him. She said, you better not say I said anything. She said, what they done, they tell you that you're booked up for a year, but Johnny Boswell is available, and Herbie ain't got a job. He says, that's what they're doing. They're calling in for Herbie Fields, and they said Johnny Boswell said, he's booked up for a year. Can't get him now. I'm telling you how they do.

So Herbie didn't say anything. He went to Joe Glazer and told Joe Glazer about it and said what was happening to him. And he said, don't worry about it. I'll break that contract, said, contract ain't worth the paper it's written on at Joe Glazer's. He got Herbie out of there and signed him up on a contract. He said, but I'm going to have to bill you.
So he put him with Hamp, and he told Hamp -- he say, I'll pay half of his salary. Hamp gave him 250.00 a week. But Joe Glazer paid 125.00 against his commission that Hamp
was paying him, and Hamp paid the other 125.00 to make his 250.00 and kept him for two years (inaudible).
Two years he was staying on the band. And Hamp would introduce him as Sergeant Herbert Fields from Fort Dix, and my name was never called in the band for five years.
